claim: A chunk arriving in the same event-loop tick the timeout becomes due is discarded (timers phase runs before poll phase).
raw: **Exact-deadline data loss (~35)** — `fetcherService.ts:342-356`: a chunk arriving in the same event-loop tick the timeout becomes due is discarded (timers phase runs before poll phase). Negligible / arguably desirable.

claim: The 60s idle timeout aborts any request where the server emits zero bytes (including SSE heartbeat comments) for >60s.
raw: **60s idle timeout aggressiveness (~55, [Unverified])** — `fetcherService.ts:310`: aborts any request where the server emits *zero* bytes (including SSE `:` heartbeat comments) for >60s. Only bites providers with no keep-alive bytes during long reasoning/tool pauses.

claim: Other for-await body consumers remain unprotected by the idle-timeout wrapper (coverage completeness).
raw: **Coverage completeness (~40, out of scope)** — other `for await (... .body)` consumers remain unprotected: `nesFetch/common/responseStream.ts`, `nesFetch/node/completionsFetchServiceImpl.ts`, `chatSessions/claude/node/claudeLanguageModelServer.ts`, `externalAgents/node/oaiLanguageModelServer.ts`.

claim: The thrown StreamIdleTimeoutError is never logged or telemetered at any of the three call sites, and processSSE's finally still logs a success-shaped 'request done' line.
raw: The thrown `StreamIdleTimeoutError` is **never logged or telemetered** at any of the three call sites. ... the `processSSE` `finally` unconditionally logs `"request done: requestId..."`, so a hung request emits a **success-shaped log line** followed by an uncategorized error.

claim: If reader.cancel() causes the in-flight read() to reject rather than resolve {done:true}, the post-try 'if (timedOut) throw' is never reached and the caller gets a raw ECONNRESET/TypeError/AbortError.
raw: If `reader.cancel()` causes the in-flight `read()` to **reject** rather than resolve `{done:true}`, `await iterator.next()` throws, unwinds through `finally`, and the post-try `if (timedOut) throw` is **never reached** — the caller gets a raw `ECONNRESET`/`TypeError`/`AbortError`.

claim: void stream.destroy().catch(() => {}) silently swallows every cleanup failure — potential silent resource leak or watchdog self-hang.
raw: `void stream.destroy().catch(() => { })` silently swallows every cleanup failure. (a) Silent resource leak if the socket abort rejects; (b) `[Inference]` potential watchdog self-hang if a backend rejects `cancel()` without settling the pending `read()`.

claim: A throwing await iterator.return?.() in the finally propagates first and masks the StreamIdleTimeoutError.
raw: A throwing `await iterator.return?.()` in the `finally` (e.g. `releaseLock()` `TypeError` with an outstanding read) propagates first and **masks** the `StreamIdleTimeoutError`. Fix: wrap `iterator.return()` in its own try/catch.

claim: The error carries duration and phase only in the message string — no request id / model / deployment — so it can't be correlated in aggregate telemetry.
raw: The error carries duration + phase only in the message string — no request id / model / deployment, unlike every neighboring telemetry call. Can't be correlated in aggregate telemetry. Fix: structured fields + optional caller-supplied context.

claim: Earlier chunks already side-effected before the throw; unchanged upstream handlers keeping accumulated partial text could present a truncated answer as complete, with no truncation marker emitted.
raw: By throw time, earlier chunks have already side-effected (`finishedCb(...)` in `stream.ts`; `feed.emitOne(...)` in the two API processors). ... unchanged upstream handlers that keep accumulated partial text could present a truncated answer as complete. No truncation marker is emitted.

claim: Underlying stream error (reject) vs. timeout is completely untested; spec never pushes an error into the stream.
raw: **G1 — underlying stream *error* (reject) vs. timeout completely untested.** The spec never pushes an error into the stream. Add a `ControllableStream.error(e)` variant; assert the iterator rejects with the real error (not `StreamIdleTimeoutError`) and `vi.getTimerCount() === 0`.

claim: Timeout error does not propagate through any call site under test; processResponseFromMessagesEndpoint has no coverage.
raw: **G2 — timeout error does not propagate through any call site under test.** `stream.ts:322`, `responsesApi.ts:537`, `messagesApi.ts:596`. ... Add fake-timer propagation tests; add any coverage for `processResponseFromMessagesEndpoint`.

claim: stream.destroy() rejection on the timeout branch is untested, and no test asserts destroy() is even called on timeout.
raw: **G3 (6)** — `stream.destroy()` rejection on the timeout branch (`fetcherService.ts:344-347`) untested; nor is it asserted that `destroy()` is even *called* on timeout. Spy on `destroy` returning a rejected promise; assert it's called, generator still throws, no unhandled rejection.

claim: Tests assert only 'first chunk'/'inactivity' substrings; a bug computing the wrong timeoutMs would pass — numeric value not asserted.
raw: **G4 (5)** — `streamIdleTimeout.spec.ts:69,94` assert only `'first chunk'`/`'inactivity'` substrings; a bug computing the wrong `timeoutMs` (e.g. `120000ms of inactivity`) would pass. Assert the numeric value too.

claim: No direct 'timer was cleared' assertion anywhere; a leaked-but-not-yet-fired timer passes silently.
raw: **G5 (5)** — no direct "timer was cleared" assertion anywhere; a leaked-but-not-yet-fired timer passes silently. Add `assert.strictEqual(vi.getTimerCount(), 0)` after normal completion (`spec:41`), slow-consumer processing (`spec:161`), and break (`spec:143`).

claim: maybeCancel cancellation-token path in stream.ts is untested (test 6 covers only a plain break).
raw: **G6 (4-5)** — `maybeCancel` cancellation-token path in `stream.ts:323` untested (test 6 covers only a plain `break`).

claim: Exact-boundary case (chunk arrives exactly at deadline) untested.
raw: **G7 (4)** — exact-boundary (chunk arrives exactly at deadline) untested.

claim: Cleanup-error masking the throw (throw outside the try/finally) is untested; worth a comment or defensive test.
raw: **G8 (4, note)** — cleanup-error masking the throw (`fetcherService.ts:371-373` outside the try/finally); low-risk for `DestroyableStream`, worth a comment/defensive test.

claim: 'consumer break releases the underlying reader lock' test doesn't verify lock release — it would still pass if the finally's iterator.return?.() were deleted.
raw: **Q1 (5)** — `spec:143-159` "consumer break releases the underlying reader lock" doesn't actually verify lock release: it would **still pass if the `finally`'s `iterator.return?.()` were deleted**, because `destroy()`→`reader.cancel()` succeeds either way.

claim: Tests 1 and 4 would pass against a trivial pass-through with all timeout logic removed (low-power).
raw: **Q2 (3, info)** — tests 1 (`spec:41`) and 4 (`spec:100`) would pass against a trivial pass-through with all timeout logic removed; real discrimination lives in tests 5 & 7.

claim: Test 7's nested fake-timer advancement is order-sensitive and would become flaky if any timer were ever armed across a yield.
raw: **Q4 (3)** — test 7's nested fake-timer advancement is order-sensitive and would become flaky if any timer were ever armed across a `yield`.

claim: JSDoc says the first-chunk timeout gets 'slightly more time' but 120s vs 60s is exactly double.
raw: **#1 — accuracy defect:** `fetcherService.ts:300-301`. JSDoc says the first-chunk timeout gets *"slightly more time,"* but 120s vs 60s is exactly **double**. A maintainer may "tidy" the windows toward each other. Rewrite to state the ratio.

claim: The 'TTFT is often longer than the subsequent chunks' comment compares a latency to chunk objects; intended comparison is against the gaps between chunks, and the premise is unverified.
raw: **#2 — imprecise rationale:** `fetcherService.ts:300-301`. *"TTFT is often longer than the subsequent chunks"* compares a latency against chunk objects; intended comparison is against the *gaps between* chunks. Also the TTFT premise is `[Inference]`.

claim: The swallowed void stream.destroy().catch(() => {}) has no rationale for the fire-and-forget or the discarded rejection.
raw: **#3:** `fetcherService.ts:346`. The swallowed `void stream.destroy().catch(() => {})` has no rationale for the fire-and-forget or the discarded rejection. Add a note.

claim: The deferred, post-finally throw (flag-then-throw-later) is the subtlest part of the design and is uncommented.
raw: **#4:** `fetcherService.ts:371-374`. The deferred, post-`finally` throw (flag-then-throw-later) is the subtlest part of the design and is uncommented; JSDoc doesn't mention the throw is deferred until after cleanup or why.

claim: The post-loop re-read of isFirstChunk looks like a stale/leftover variable without a note explaining it deliberately reflects the timed-out phase.
raw: **#5:** `fetcherService.ts:372`. The post-loop re-read of `isFirstChunk` looks like a stale/leftover variable without a note explaining it deliberately reflects the phase that timed out.

claim: The 'Creates a DestroyableStream…' docstring sits on the interface (a shape that creates nothing) instead of on createControllableStream.
raw: **#6:** `streamIdleTimeout.spec.ts:10-13`. The "Creates a DestroyableStream…" docstring sits on the `interface` (a shape, which creates nothing) instead of on `createControllableStream`. Move or reword it.

claim: withStreamIdleTimeout JSDoc omits the same-tick race edge (chunk yielded before the error surfaces).
raw: **#7 (optional):** `fetcherService.ts:321-327`. JSDoc omits the same-tick race edge; fine to leave, flagged so it's a conscious choice.

claim: The positional 'the timer is cleared above' comment will drift silently if code moves (comment-rot risk).
raw: **Comment-rot risks:** the "slightly more time" prose (`:301`, already wrong) and the positional "the timer is cleared above" (`:363`) will drift silently if code moves.

claim: Phase not exposed as data — first-chunk/idle distinction lives only in message, forcing brittle err.message.includes(...) parsing.
raw: 1. **Phase not exposed as data — `fetcherService.ts:312-319`.** First-chunk/idle distinction lives only in `message`, forcing brittle `err.message.includes(...)` parsing (spec ~lines 69, 93). Fix: replace the `isFirstChunk` boolean with `public readonly phase: 'awaiting-first-chunk' | 'inactivity'`.

claim: timeoutMs is discarded — consumed into the message string and unreadable; should be a public readonly field.
raw: 2. **`timeoutMs` discarded — `fetcherService.ts:313-317`.** Diagnostic value consumed into the string and unreadable. Fix: `public readonly timeoutMs: number`. (1+2 are one constructor change.)

claim: Return type AsyncGenerator<T> is too wide — leaks .return/.throw/TNext/any-return no caller uses.
raw: 3. **Return type `AsyncGenerator<T>` too wide — `fetcherService.ts:330`.** Leaks `.return`/`.throw`/`TNext`/`any`-return no caller uses. Fix: `AsyncIterableIterator<T>` (or `AsyncIterable<T>`).

claim: Input constrained to concrete DestroyableStream<T> — couples the watchdog to one class and complicates testing.
raw: 4. **Input constrained to concrete `DestroyableStream<T>` — `fetcherService.ts:329`.** Couples the watchdog to one class and complicates testing. Fix: structural `AsyncIterable<T> & { destroy(): Promise<void> }`.

claim: Timeout policy hardcoded to module constants — not injectable; tests must use real 60s/120s durations.
raw: 5. **Timeout policy hardcoded to module constants — `fetcherService.ts:354`.** Not injectable; tests must use real 60s/120s durations. Fix: optional `StreamIdleTimeoutOptions` defaulting to the constants.

claim: Constructor (number, boolean) allows a mismatched phase/timeout pair (illegal states representable).
raw: 6. **Constructor allows mismatched phase/timeout pair — `fetcherService.ts:313`.** `(number, boolean)` accepts illegal combos; largely addressed by finding 1.

claim: Bare-number constants express no relationship between the first-chunk and idle timeouts.
raw: 7. **Bare-`number` constants express no relationship — `:303`, `:310`.** Minor; optionally fold into one default-policy object. A branded duration type would be over-engineering.

claim: Generic T carries no intent; cosmetically rename to TChunk.
raw: 8. **Generic `T` carries no intent — `:328`.** Cosmetic; rename to `TChunk`.

claim: 'slightly more time' mischaracterizes a 2x difference (120s vs 60s is exactly double).
raw: The JSDoc says the first-chunk timeout gets "slightly more time." The values are `SSE_FIRST_CHUNK_TIMEOUT_MS = 2 * 60 * 1000` (120s, line 303) versus `SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 * 1000` (60s, line 310). That is exactly **double** — 100% more, not "slightly more."

claim: TTFT rationale wording is imprecise (compares latency to chunk objects, not the gaps between chunks) and the premise is unverified.
raw: "The model's TTFT is often longer than the subsequent chunks" compares a latency (time-to-first-token) against "the subsequent chunks" (objects), when the intended comparison is against *the gaps between* subsequent chunks. ... the premise itself ... is [Inference].

claim: The swallowed destroy().catch(() => {}) has no rationale for the void fire-and-forget or the discarded rejection.
raw: `void stream.destroy().catch(() => { });` runs inside the timer callback with no comment. Two non-obvious decisions are silent here: (a) the `void` fire-and-forget (the callback can't await), and (b) why any rejection from `destroy()` is intentionally discarded.

claim: The deferred, post-finally throw (flag-then-throw-later) is the crux of the design and has no explanation.
raw: On timeout the code doesn't throw from the timer; it sets `timedOut`, destroys the stream ..., lets the loop exit, runs cleanup in `finally`, and only then throws. This flag-then-throw-later mechanism is the crux of the design and has no explanation.

claim: The post-loop re-read of isFirstChunk looks accidental/stale without a note that it deliberately reflects the timed-out phase.
raw: `isFirstChunk` is the loop's phase selector, but it's read again after the loop to pick which timeout value/message the error reports. A reader can easily mistake this for a stale/leftover variable rather than a deliberate reuse.

claim: Test interface docstring describes creation but is attached to interface ControllableStream, not to createControllableStream.
raw: The JSDoc "Creates a DestroyableStream backed by a ReadableStream…" sits on `interface ControllableStream<T>` (line 14), but an interface creates nothing — it's the return-shape. The actual creating is done by `createControllableStream` (line 20), which has no doc.

claim: withStreamIdleTimeout JSDoc omits the same-tick race edge (a chunk landing on the timer tick can still be yielded).
raw: Strictly, if a chunk lands in the same tick the timer fires, that chunk can still be yielded before the error surfaces on the next `done`. This is fine to leave out (it's an edge and would add noise), but flagging so the omission is a conscious choice rather than an oversight.

claim: 'the timer is cleared above' is a positional reference to line 356 that goes stale if clearTimer() moves (comment rot).
raw: `...fetcherService.ts:363` — "the timer is cleared above" is a positional reference to line 356. If the `clearTimer()` call is moved (or a second `startTimer` is introduced before the yield), the comment goes stale with no compiler warning.

claim: The {@link ...} references won't fail the build if a target is renamed — they'd become dead links (low risk).
raw: The `{@link ...}` references (lines 322-326) are good for navigation but won't fail the build if a target is renamed — they'd become dead links. Low risk, acceptable.

claim: Underlying stream error (reject) vs. timeout is completely untested; the spec never pushes an error into the stream, so real-error surfacing and timer-clear-on-error are unverified.
raw: `streamIdleTimeout.spec.ts` never pushes an *error* into the stream. ... if `iterator.next()` rejects ..., the **original** error propagates (the `throw` at line 371-373 is skipped). Nothing verifies: that the real error surfaces unchanged ... and that the watchdog timer is cleared.

claim: Timeout error propagation through the three call sites is untested; messagesApi's processResponseFromMessagesEndpoint has no processor-level test at all.
raw: no test confirms a `StreamIdleTimeoutError` actually surfaces to a consumer of the three call sites ... `messagesApi`'s `processResponseFromMessagesEndpoint` has no processor-level test at all.

claim: stream.destroy() rejection on the timeout branch is untested, and no test asserts destroy() is actually called on timeout.
raw: the timer callback does `void stream.destroy().catch(() => { })`. No test drives a `destroy()` that rejects, so the swallow-and-still-throw behavior is unverified; nor does any test assert `destroy()` is actually *called* on timeout.

claim: Error-message tests assert only 'first chunk'/'inactivity' substrings, never the numeric timeoutMs, so a wrong-timeoutMs bug would pass.
raw: Tests at `streamIdleTimeout.spec.ts:69` and `:94` only assert the substrings `'first chunk'` / `'inactivity'`. ... a bug computing the wrong `timeoutMs` — e.g. reporting `120000ms of inactivity` — would pass the current assertion.

claim: No direct assertion that the timer is cleared (vi.getTimerCount() === 0); a leaked timer that doesn't fire in-window passes silently.
raw: None assert `vi.getTimerCount() === 0` after normal completion (`spec:41`), during/after slow-consumer processing (`spec:161`...), or after break (`spec:143`). A timer that leaks but happens not to fire during the test window would pass silently today.

claim: maybeCancel cancellation-token interaction in stream.ts is untested; test 6 covers only a plain break.
raw: `stream.ts:323` calls `this.maybeCancel('after awaiting body chunk')` ...; a `true` result `return`s from the loop, which must unwind `withStreamIdleTimeout`'s `finally` ... and release the reader. Test 6 covers a plain `break`, but not the cancellation-token path

claim: The exact-boundary case (chunk arrives exactly at deadline) is untested.
raw: The chunk-arrives-exactly-at-deadline case (advance exactly `SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, then push) — where timer-vs-chunk ordering is ambiguous — is not pinned. Low value but cheap to add.

claim: Cleanup-error masking the timeout throw is untested — a rejecting iterator.return?.() in the finally would replace the StreamIdleTimeoutError.
raw: `fetcherService.ts:371-373`'s `throw` sits *outside* the `try/finally`. If `await iterator.return?.()` in the `finally` (line 368) ever rejects, that rejection replaces the `StreamIdleTimeoutError`. For `DestroyableStream` this is low-risk ... but it's worth a one-line comment or a defensive test.

claim: 'consumer break releases the underlying reader lock' test doesn't verify lock release — it would still pass if the finally's iterator.return?.() were deleted.
raw: After the `break`, the only post-condition is that `await stream.destroy()` (line 158) resolves. ... **this test would still pass even if the `finally`'s `iterator.return?.()` (`fetcherService.ts:368`) were deleted**, i.e. it does not actually guard the behavior in its name.

claim: Tests 1 and 4 are low-power pass-through checks that would pass against a trivial yield* with all timeout logic removed.
raw: `spec:41` ("yields all chunks") and `spec:100` ("does not time out within the deadline") would both pass against a trivial `yield*` pass-through with all timeout logic removed. They are fine as happy-path smoke tests but provide no independent protection for the watchdog.

claim: Test 7's intricate nested fake-timer advancement is order-sensitive and would become flaky if the implementation ever kept a timer armed across a yield.
raw: Test 7 (`spec:161-186`) has the background consumer call `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS * 3)` *inside* its loop while the main flow also advances timers. ... would become order-sensitive/flaky if the implementation ever kept any timer armed across a `yield`.

claim: Phase is not exposed as data — the first-chunk/idle distinction lives only in message, forcing err.message.includes(...) parsing.
raw: 1. **Phase is not exposed as data — `fetcherService.ts:312-319`.** The first-chunk/idle distinction lives only in `message`, forcing `err.message.includes('first chunk' | 'inactivity')` parsing (spec ~lines 69, 93). Fix: add `public readonly phase: 'awaiting-first-chunk' | 'inactivity'`.

claim: timeoutMs is discarded — consumed into the string and unreadable afterward; should be a public readonly field.
raw: 2. **`timeoutMs` is discarded — `fetcherService.ts:313-317`.** The elapsed-timeout diagnostic value is consumed into the string and unreadable afterward. Fix: `public readonly timeoutMs: number`.

claim: Return type AsyncGenerator<T> is too wide — leaks .return/.throw/TNext/any-return that no caller uses.
raw: 3. **Return type `AsyncGenerator<T>` is too wide — `fetcherService.ts:330`.** Leaks `.return`/`.throw`/`TNext`/`any`-return that no caller uses. Fix: return `AsyncIterableIterator<T>` (or `AsyncIterable<T>`).

claim: Input is constrained to the concrete DestroyableStream<T>, coupling the watchdog to one class and complicating testing.
raw: 4. **Input constrained to the concrete `DestroyableStream<T>` — `fetcherService.ts:329`.** Couples the watchdog to one class and complicates testing. Fix: accept a structural `AsyncIterable<T> & { destroy(): Promise<void> }`.

claim: Timeout policy is hardcoded to module constants, not injectable; tests must use the real production durations.
raw: 5. **Timeout policy hardcoded to module constants — `fetcherService.ts:354`.** Not injectable; tests must use the real production durations. Fix: optional `StreamIdleTimeoutOptions` defaulting to the two constants.

claim: Constructor accepts a mismatched phase/timeout pair — (number, boolean) allows illegal combinations like idle ms with isFirstChunk=true.
raw: 6. **Constructor allows a mismatched phase/timeout pair — `fetcherService.ts:313`.** `(number, boolean)` accepts illegal combinations (e.g. idle ms with `isFirstChunk = true`). Addressed largely by finding 1.

claim: The bare-number constants express no relationship (ordering, positivity) between first-chunk and idle timeouts.
raw: 7. **Bare-`number` constants express no relationship — `fetcherService.ts:303`, `:310`.** Minor. Optionally fold into a single default policy object ...; a branded duration type would be over-engineering here.

claim: Generic T carries no intent; cosmetically rename to TChunk (the SSE byte-chunk type).
raw: 8. **Generic `T` carries no intent — `fetcherService.ts:328`.** Cosmetic. Rename to `TChunk` (and optionally document it as the SSE byte-chunk type) for readability; no behavioral change.

claim: The timeout error is thrown but never logged or telemetered; in stream.ts the surrounding finally logs a misleading success-shaped 'request done'.
raw: the timeout error is thrown but never logged or sent to telemetry; in `stream.ts` the surrounding `finally` actively logs a misleading "request done" ... a hung/aborted request emits a success-shaped "request done" log line, then an uncategorized error bubbles up with no correlating error log.

claim: If iterator.next() rejects on cancel, the exception unwinds and the post-try 'if (timedOut) throw StreamIdleTimeoutError' is never executed — the caller receives the raw reject reason.
raw: if `reader.cancel()` instead causes the in-flight `read()` to *reject* ..., then `await iterator.next()` throws. That exception unwinds through the `finally` ... and the `if (timedOut) throw new StreamIdleTimeoutError(...)` block, sitting *after* the try/finally, is never executed.

claim: void stream.destroy().catch(() => {}) swallows every cleanup failure — a resource leak or a watchdog that itself hangs becomes completely silent.
raw: `void stream.destroy().catch(() => { })` swallows every cleanup failure — a resource leak (or a watchdog that itself hangs) becomes completely silent ... 1. Silent resource leak ... 2. [Inference] Watchdog self-hang if a non-spec-compliant backend rejects `cancel()` without settling the read.

claim: A throwing iterator.return?.() in the finally propagates first and preempts the intended StreamIdleTimeoutError (e.g. releaseLock() TypeError).
raw: because the timeout throw lives *after* the try/finally, any rejection from `await iterator.return?.()` propagates first and preempts the `StreamIdleTimeoutError`. `DestroyableStream`'s async iterator `finally` calls `reader.releaseLock()`, which throws a `TypeError` if a read is still outstanding.

claim: StreamIdleTimeoutError carries no request/model/deployment context, so even when surfaced it can't be correlated in telemetry.
raw: the message ... states duration and phase but not *which* request timed out. Every neighboring log/telemetry call in `stream.ts` is keyed on `requestId.headerRequestId` and `deploymentId`; this error has neither, so it can't be tied to an endpoint, model, or request id.

claim: Partial data already delivered (finishedCb/feed.emitOne) before the throw could be accepted as a complete response downstream; no truncation marker is emitted.
raw: by the time the timeout throws, earlier chunks have already been fed to the SSE parser and side-effected ... any top-level handler that catches the thrown error but keeps the already-accumulated partial text ... would present a truncated answer as complete. ... it also doesn't emit a marker.

claim: Exact-deadline data loss: a chunk delivered in the same event-loop iteration the timeout becomes due is discarded (timers phase runs before poll phase).
raw: **Exact-deadline data loss (confidence ~35).** `fetcherService.ts:342-356`: if a chunk is delivered in the *same* event-loop iteration the timeout becomes due, Node runs the timers phase before the poll phase, so the watchdog fires first, destroys the stream, and discards that just-arrived chunk.

claim: The 60s idle timeout will abort any request where the server goes fully silent (zero bytes, including heartbeat comments) for >60s — a tuning risk for providers with no keep-alive bytes.
raw: **60s idle timeout aggressiveness (confidence ~55, [Unverified]).** `SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (fetcherService.ts:310) will abort any request where the server goes fully silent — emitting *zero* bytes, including SSE `:` heartbeat comments — for >60s.

claim: Other for-await body consumers in the copilot extension remain unprotected by the idle-timeout wrapper (coverage completeness, out of diff scope).
raw: **Coverage completeness (confidence ~40, out of the changed-lines scope).** ... other `for await (... .body)` consumers in the copilot extension (e.g. `.../nesFetch/common/responseStream.ts`, `.../completionsFetchServiceImpl.ts`, ...) that remain unprotected.
